page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7T83 processor clocked at 2.55 GHz, this instance features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 dedicated physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). It is equipped with 32 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache specifications include 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, while AVX-512 extensions are omitted.

The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps and includes no bundled local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark evaluations show solid middle-tier compute output, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 21,424.46 and single-core reaching 2,679.28. Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics sit at 1,500.0 and 8,253.0 respectively, with software compilation reaching 13,374.0 points. While small-block cached memory bandwidth operates at 1,028.21 GB/sec, uncached large-block memory performance drops to 23.77 GB/sec for reads and 12.96 GB/sec for writes, indicating a memory throughput bottleneck under heavy streaming data access.

Featuring a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the ecs.c7a.4xlarge offers high compute density for core-bound tasks without allocating unused memory reserves. Small-model LLM text generation shows strong throughput at 301.48 tokens/sec for 135M models, while Redis SET operations sustain 15.82 million operations per second. However, the absence of local storage requires attachment of external block storage for persistent data operations. The combination of dedicated AMD cores and low memory ratio makes this instance well-suited for web serving, software compilation pipelines, application backends, and moderate CPU-focused data processing tasks.
description: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance equipped with an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores at 2.55 GHz. Built on an x86_64 architecture with 32 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU), it delivers a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio suitable for compute-heavy applications. The instance features a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, no bundled local storage, and no included GPUs. Benchmark testing reveals steady general compute performance, including a PassMark CPU score of 21,196.32 and 15.82 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside strong 135M model LLM text generation at 301.48 tokens/sec. However, uncached memory write speed is limited to 12.96 GB/sec. This instance provides a balanced hardware footprint for CPU-bound microservices, software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight model inference.
